chapter: First big band, his father, arriving in Kansas City
title: Walking everywhere, feeding the hogs and curing pork
summary: He recalls walking miles each day, carrying feed to his uncle's hogs, and the family curing pork in the wash house.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I did have a bicycle later on, but I mean, I'm speaking about the years -- well, I didn't get the bicycle until, I guess, a year or two before I come out of high school, see? But all that other stuff was purely everything you did, you walked.

Now, we used to have hogs, you know, that -- you know, we fed, you know. Well, we stayed in town, so consequently we couldn't keep the hogs over there where we stayed. So we'd have to keep the hogs over to our uncle's, which was a mile and a half from where we stayed. Well, my dad would have the feed at our house and I would have to take the feed and mix the feed up after I get over to my uncle's and feed the hogs, instead of -- you know what I mean? See? And I'd have to pack that feed a mile and a half when I get up in the morning and come back a mile and a half home.
That's everyday. Then walk a mile and a half to school and a mile and a half back after school was out. Now, back that evening to feed the hogs a mile and a half, back that night.
What would that feed be in? What would you carry it in?
You must have been very strong in those days.

-- you could do a lot of things that -- you know what I mean, that you wouldn't think you could do, you know? But you got to do them, because -- but I -- he told me that was my job. That's what I had to do. But now, see, this was one particular year, especially the year when we raised hogs. When we raised the hogs, well, then, we'd kill them and that would be enough meat to carry us for another year. But I'd have to do that about every other year.
What you mean, the meat carried us for --
When we killed a hog, that carried us for a year, without having to buy meat.
Well, you salt it and you cure it.
See? Salt it and you cure it and so then --
We had what you call a wash house, see, and that's where we kept the meat, in the wash house.
Yeah, it looks like a garage, like where you drive a car in.
But then it would be hanging?
Yeah, hang it up in the top.
And so then it would be salt pork.
Salt pork and all that kind of stuff.
So what we did, see now, where the meat was up in there, I had a trap where I could get up there to get to it, but see, I had a thing like that underneath. See what I mean?
